articles.title: 2026 MLB Playoff Format: How Many Teams, Wild Card Seeding, More
articles.summary: Learn how the 2026 MLB playoffs work, including the 12-team field, Wild Card Series, seeding, byes, tiebreakers and World Series home-field advantage.
articles.body: Twelve teams get a shot at October. Only one finishes it with a World Series title. The MLB postseason sends six American League clubs and six National League clubs into a four-round bracket. The top two division winners in each league earn a bye. Everyone else has to survive a best-of-three Wild Card Series before the bracket shifts into the longer rounds. The 2026 postseason is tentatively scheduled to begin Tuesday, Sept. 29. The World Series is scheduled to open Friday, Oct. 23 on FOX. Fans can stream the National League Division Series, National League Championship Series and World Series games carried on FOX and FS1 with FOX One. How Many Teams Reach the MLB Playoffs? Twelve teams qualify, six from each league. That means all three division winners from the AL and NL make the field, along with three Wild Card teams from each league. How Are MLB Playoff Teams Seeded? Each league uses the same six-seed structure: The biggest regular-season reward belongs to the Nos. 1 and 2 seeds: a direct trip to the Division Series. The No. 3 seed hosts the No. 6 seed, while the No. 4 seed hosts the No. 5 seed in the Wild Card Series. Division titles still carry weight. A Wild Card team can finish with a better record than a division winner and still receive a lower seed. How Many Rounds Are in the MLB Playoffs? The postseason has four rounds: How Does the Wild Card Series Work? There is no one-game escape hatch anymore. The Wild Card round is a best-of-three series scheduled across three consecutive days, with the higher-seeded team hosting every game. The No. 3 seed plays the No. 6 seed and the No. 4 seed plays the No. 5 seed in each league. The winners advance to the Division Series. Are Teams Reseeded After the Wild Card Series? No. Once the bracket is set, it stays set. The winner of the No. 4-No. 5 matchup advances to face the No. 1 seed, while the winner of the No. 3-No. 6 matchup advances to face the No. 2 seed. How Long Is Each MLB Playoff Series? The Division Series uses a 2-2-1 home format. The League Championship Series and World Series use a 2-3-2 format. How Do MLB Postseason Tiebreakers Work? Game 163 is gone. If teams finish tied for a division title or playoff spot, MLB settles it mathematically, beginning with head-to-head record. If the tie remains, the league moves through additional criteria including intradivision record and interdivision record. Who Gets Home-Field Advantage in the World Series? The league champion with the better regular-season record receives home-field advantage in the World Series, regardless of its postseason seed. If the teams finished with identical records, MLB applies its tiebreaker system. Are Postseason Extra-Inning Rules Different? Yes. October baseball drops the automatic runner at second base in extra innings, so teams have to manufacture the winning run from scratch. Managers also begin postseason games with two replay challenges instead of one. That is the postseason pressure test: 12 teams enter, four earn an opening-round bye and the other eight face three games or fewer to keep their season alive.

articles.title: All 21 Of Lionel Messi's FIFA World Cup Goals, Ranked
articles.summary: The GOAT just keeps reminding us he's the GOAT. Here are all of Lionel Messi's goals at the World Cup, best to the very best.
articles.body: Editor's note: This story was originally published July 20, 2026. Lionel Messi continues to remind the football world that he's the greatest player of all time, with one GOAT move after another. He's the all-time leading FIFA World Cup goalscorer — and will only extend his mark with every goal. And that he is doing it 20 years after first setting foot at the World Cup is even more remarkable. There is no doubt that the Argentinian captain, who is playing in a record sixth World Cup alongside Cristiano Ronaldo, will continue to keep opponents up at night. Messi now stands alone in FIFA World Cup history with 21 tournament goals and 123 overall as Argentina's top scorer. But it can’t just end there, so allow me to rank all 21 goals across all World Cups that he has scored. Because every beautiful gem deserves its own appraisal: 21. Goal vs. Saudi Arabia | Nov. 22, 2022 Messi stepped up for the penalty after a foul on Leandro Paredes. But the shock of the tournament arrived when Herve Renard’s Saudi Arabia came out victorious. It would only be the spark that would eventually kickstart a historic World Cup-winning campaign. 20. First Goal vs. France | Dec. 18, 2022 For me, the 2022 World Cup final was the greatest I have ever witnessed, and it started with another spot-kick as Messi made it 1-0. Little did we know that this would only be the first chapter of an incredible footballing novel. 19. Goal vs. Netherlands | Dec. 9, 2022 Messi already had an assist for the opening goal, and he made it 2-0 before the Netherlands came back to make it very entertaining with another penalty. La Pulga placed it beautifully past Andries Noppert as the Argentina faithful celebrated from behind the goal. 18. Goal vs. Croatia | Dec. 13, 2022 Another clutch penalty after Julián Álvarez was taken down. Messi’s spot-kick was smashed into the top right corner as Dominik Livaković couldn’t do anything about it. 17. Second Goal vs. France | Dec. 18, 2022 A dramatic goal in stoppage time when Argentina took a 3-2 lead as Hugo Lloris failed to push away a shot from Lautaro Martinez, so Messi pounced. As we all remember, the night would conclude with a penalty shootout and a glorious third World Cup title, 36 years after Diego Maradona lifted the trophy in México. 16. Second Goal vs. Algeria | June 16, 2026 A prototypical Messi instinct is to react before anyone else. And that’s what happened here after Alexis Mac Allister’s effort was pushed away by Zidane, but not far enough. Messi pounced and earned his second goal of the night. 15. Goal vs. Jordan | June 28, 2026 Argentina, already through and having won the group, started without Messi, who did not need to play a whole 90 minutes. As if he ever needs a full match to create some magic. Leo entered the action in the 60th minute, and 20 minutes later, he scored his second free kick at a World Cup and his 19th career goal at the tournament. It was a great finish, though I think the keeper and his wall could have done better. From another angle, you can also see Argentina’s stopper Emiliano "Dibu" Martínez conducting the Argentinian wall and telling them where to stand in order for Messi to find his path towards goal. It’s brilliant. As a result, Messi also became the first men’s player to score in seven straight World Cup matches. 14. Third Goal vs. Algeria | June 16, 2026 There is probably more of a poetic, symbolic meaning to this goal as it officially marked his first ever hat trick at the World Cup. But it was also a delightful finish that sealed the three points and placed Messi in the history books. Receiving a ball from Nico Gonzalez inside the box, the soon-to-be 39-year-old star made a quick assessment and shot at Zidane with an effort that went bottom-left. Once again, the goal was perfectly placed with tremendous accuracy and the stadium knew the outcome. We all did. Messi, once again, gave us an evening to never forget. 13. Goal vs. Australia | Dec. 3, 2022 It took a dramatic save from Emiliano Martínez at the end of this one for Argentina to secure the victory, but it all started with Messi’s opener during what was his 1,000th career match. The goal started from a free-kick cross by Leo that ended up with him entering the box and, with a slight touch from Nicolas Otamendi, the Argentinian icon placed a low shot past Matt Ryan. 12. First Goal vs. Algeria | June 16, 2026 Messi, as he is turning, receives the ball from his Inter Miami teammate Rodrigo De Paul, and with his quintessential, almost omnipotent left foot, takes an effort just outside the box, smashing a powerful shot past Algeria’s Luka Zidane. Zinedine’s son probably saw it coming, but like many other mortals, it just can’t be stopped. It was the door that opened the floodgates. Once again, as is always the case, it started and ended with Messi as he provided the ball out to the left to Julian Alvarez. The man from Atlético de Madrid saw his shot saved, Messi claimed it, then shot it. THAT one gets blocked, but because Leo never quits, the Argentinian captain headed toward the center of the box and smashed it in. Pure determination. 11. Record-Breaking Goal vs. Austria | June 22, 2026 Of course, this is the goal that's sealed in time, making him the all-time scorer in men's World Cup history. After missing a penalty in the 14th minute, Messi made amends by scoring a delicious finish, thanks also to a wonderful dummy by Thiago Almada. Messi took it the first time, and it was clear he was never going to miss. On the 40th anniversary of Diego Maradona’s "Hand of God" against England in the 1986 World Cup quarterfinal, Messi created another eternal memory for Argentina. 10. Goal vs. Serbia and Montenegro | June 16, 2006 Messi’s first ever goal at the World Cup. Days before his 19th birthday, Messi came on from the bench with just over 15 minutes left. Carlos Tevez found the then-Barcelona teenager, who made a run inside the box and slotted it past the goalkeeper. It may not be his greatest goal from an aesthetic perspective, but it’s one of the most meaningful. 9. Goal vs. Mexico | Nov. 26, 2022 Anxiety was rising with Argentina fans as La Albiceleste was currently at 0-0 against Mexico deep in the second half. But then came Leo as Di María gave him the ball just outside the box. The Argentina captain sent a powerful, low effort past Memo Ochoa for the opener and the South Americans erupted. 8. Goal vs. Cape Verde | July 3rd, 2026 Lisandro Martínez deserves a lot of credit for this goal as it was his deep, beautiful assist that fed Messi inside Cabo Verde’s box. The Argentinian captain brought it down beautifully with his left foot and in the same breath, placed it past Vozinha – perhaps the only other player at the tournament who has captured so much attention at this tournament. This goal made it eight consecutive World Cup matches, extending his own record for the longest streak ever. 7. Goal vs. Egypt | Round of 16 | July 7, 2026 The equalizing goal that shook Atlanta’s stadium and sent it into ecstasy. Leo himself pings the ball in the box but it scrambles away until Gonzalo Montiel finds it and just about returns it to Messi, who proceeds to smash it past Egypt’s stopper Mostafa Shobeir. It hits the crossbar and eventually ricochets into the net. A magnificent finish at such a crucial moment. 6. First Goal vs. Nigeria | June 25, 2014 Messi ended the group stage in perfection, scoring a brace against Nigeria. The first came in the second minute of action as Angel Di María hit the post and, like a bull charging at will, Leo entered the box and smashed it in. An absolute rocket. 5. Second Goal vs. Austria | June 22, 2026 Once again, as is always the case, it started and ended with Messi as he provided the ball out to the left to Julian Alvarez. The man from Atlético de Madrid saw his shot saved, Messi claimed it, then shot it. THAT one gets blocked, but because Leo never quits, the Argentinian captain headed toward the center of the box and smashed it in. Pure determination. And also, pay attention to his touch just as he gets the ball inside the box. It is the definition of genius and elegance. But you have to slow down the highlight in order to truly appreciate it. 4. Second Goal vs. Nigeria | June 25, 2014 The second was Messi’s first and only free-kick goal at the World Cup. Nigeria came back with a goal but, in true fashion, La Pulga reclaimed his team the lead with a beautiful set piece. Nigeria goalkeeper Vincent Enyeama could only watch and follow it in as he knew — as we all did — he was already beaten. 3. Goal vs. Iran | June 21, 2014 Iran held on as much as it could. But when you face Messi, that’s just never enough. In the 90th minute, Leo picked up the ball on the edge of the box and completely smashed a beautiful left-footed attempt heading towards the top left of goal. A piece of magic and one of my favorite goals. 2. Goal vs. Bosnia and Herzegovina | June 15, 2014 Messi didn’t score in the 2010 World Cup so he had to make amends four years later in Brazil. At 27, he was ready to make a statement and this is one of my favorite goals because you are now seeing prime Leo—running at full speed—unable to be stopped. Messi drives towards goal, gives it to Gonzalo Higuain, gets it right back and, with a lethal left-foot finish that eventually becomes a trademark on the bottom left, scores. The best part is that he forced two Bosnian defenders to crash into each other in the process, as they were unable to stop the Argentinian. They became two early victims of Messi’s wrath. 1. Goal vs. Nigeria | June 26, 2018 After causing havoc against the Super Eagles back in 2014, the African side was probably done with this guy by the time Russia 2018 arrived. But Messi was not and four years later, Leo scored what is in my opinion, his greatest World Cup goal. He received a great pass from Ever Banega, and as he was tracked down by a defender, Leo took a touch as smooth as butter with his left knee, then with his left foot, brought it down to his weaker right foot and slammed it past the goalkeeper. Hang it in the Louvre? It’s a goal so good that it deserves to have its own exhibition.

articles.title: Cody Gakpo transfer news: Man City consider options after Liverpool reject £80m bid for winger
articles.summary: Man City consider options after Liverpool reject £80m bid Cody Gakpo; City interested in Everton winger Iliman Ndiaye, who is in advanced talks with Tottenham; City allowed Savio and Omar Marmoush to join Tottenham this month, and Jack Grealish is of interest to Everton and Sunderland
articles.body:
Sky Sports News understands Liverpool were concerned about their chances of bringing in a replacement for the Dutchman.

As things stand, they are unwilling to let him leave in this transfer window - which then brought City back into play for Ndiaye.

Discussions are moving swiftly after City were knocked back for Gakpo, with Spurs having previously established a fee of £60m with Everton for Ndiaye and contact already established between City and Everton over Jack Grealish.

Everton are believed to be Grealish's preferred destination. He also has interest from Sunderland. Manchester City want to sign a wide forward and a central midfielder before the window closes.

They are interested in Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez .

Manchester City allowed Savio and Omar Marmoush to join Tottenham earlier month, reducing Enzo Maresca's options on the wing.

City did not name a winger on their bench in Friday's win over Crystal Palace and started with Phil Foden - who Enzo Maresca admitted is not a winger - out wide at Selhurst Park.

Liverpool signed Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain on Monday while Victor Munoz arrived from Osasuna earlier this summer.

Spurs also targeted Gakpo in this window before signing Savio and Marmoush.

articles.title: Fantasy football impact of NFL placing Packers RB Josh Jacobs on commissioner exempt list
articles.summary: Hayden Winks examines how fantasy managers should navigate the Packers offense in the aftermath of Josh Jacobs being place on commissioner exempt list.
articles.body:
Packers running back Josh Jacobs was placed on the commissioner's exempt list on Sunday , stemming from an alleged battery at his home. The district attorney's office charged him with two misdemeanor charges and released a report of the incident.

In that report , there is indication of surveillance video that corroborates with the victim's testimony of battery and destruction of property (her cell phone). Historically, the NFL tends to wait until the legal process plays out before suspending a player, but one way that process gets expedited is with video evidence. It's unclear if the NFL has seen this video or if it is concerned about it leaking, but it would not be a surprise if this evidence landed Jacobs on the commissioner's exempt list even though his first day in court isn't until November and even though his legal case is more likely to be concluded in 2027.

How many games Jacobs will miss is to be determined.

The Jabrill Peppers case in 2024 is similar. Peppers was accused of domestic violence, and he was placed on the commissioner's exempt list even though his legal case hadn't been finalized. He missed the first seven games of the season , and he was removed from the list then because NFL rules call for a six-game suspension for a first offense of domestic violence. If he stayed on the list for beyond the six games, then he'd be serving a longer suspension than what is outlined. This would be the precedent for Jacobs being suspended for the first six or so games of 2026.

Of course, that's just one way this can play out. Jacobs can come off the list at any point, and he can stay on it for longer than the 6-7 games that was suggested above. What is on the video and if it will be released to the public could play into how long his absence will be. That could also play into if the Packers want to hold onto him this season. The Packers stated that they expect Jacobs to be a Packer in 2026 , but things could change with public pressure.

Jacobs could not miss any time in 2026 in theory. This would be equally surprising, as Jacobs could've avoided the commissioner's exempt list. The range for games missed this year truly is 0-17 with the most likely scenario being around the six games outlined by the personal conduct policy. It's now far more likely to happen in September and October.

When strictly talking about Jacobs the football player, he would likely be viewed as the Packers' starter upon return, but his status of a clear-cut bellcow is more in doubt with Marshawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Chris Brooks available to emerge while he's away from practice and game action. Jacobs was the RB12 on RB10 usage last fantasy football season as the clear-cut starter. That's closer to his ceiling in games when he's available. I'm assuming he's in the RB12-18 range from Week 7 on, as an upside fantasy RB2. It's a bit easier to find replacements before bye weeks and before injuries pile up, but Jacobs is impossible to justify going ahead of Jadarian Price, Bucky Irving and others with season-long upside without likely missing time. Jacobs is my 72nd overall player and RB28 in half PPR right now, just after Jaylen Warren and Rhamondre Stevenson types. Those examples face in-house competition and have less league-winning upside than Jacobs.

Lloyd was a great insurance target before news broke, yet was drafted on only 10% of Yahoo leagues heading into the weekend. He should be (and will be) drafted in 100% of Yahoo drafts moving forward. Lloyd was a real prospect and went in the third round of the NFL Draft as a bigger back with pass-catching experience and quality athleticism. Soft-tissue injuries stemming from a college knee injury zapped his playing time early in his career, but Lloyd has been healthy throughout the offseason and he has solidified himself as the Packers' RB2 ahead of pass-protecting fullback hybrid Chris Brooks.

Lloyd has upside RB2 value without Jacobs active. That profile deserves to be priced well ahead of theoretical insurance types, as it appears he will get a month or so of starts. I moved him to 92nd overall and RB34 in half PPR, right next to Rams RB2 Blake Corum and Steelers 1B Rico Dowdle. There's risk in Lloyd not getting a bellcow role with newly-acquired Kaleb Johnson being an outside zone early-down option, or if Lloyd's injury history is too extensive to immediately graduate him to nearly 20 touches per game. About sixish games of RB20 value to start the year unlocks riskier builds, like drafting TreVeyon Henderson, Jonathon Brooks or more hero RB teams.

It's possible to draft Jacobs and Lloyd together if either fall beyond the 72nd and 92nd overall rankings that I outlined here. It's a conservative approach, but the Packers' starting RB role has been valuable for years.

On the margins, Jacobs' projected absence helps out Jordan Love, Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, Jayden Reed and Tucker Kraft as well. Since 2024 when Jacobs joined the Packers, they've been 31st in neutral pass rate and 31st in neutral pace. It's been one of the most conservative offenses, which has limited the entire pass game. That likely changes now. Love and this young, explosive skill group is ripe for more trust. The coaching staff has expressed operating faster out of the huddle during the offseason, and the Packers played that way with the starters earlier in the preseason. More plays and more pass attempts is how Love, Golden and Reed can pay off as fantasy sleepers . The fact that they aren't rotating a WR4 and WR5 this year is equally important.

The Packers are the team I've drafted the most this offseason. That's not going to change in my remaining drafts.

articles.title: Could Erik Karlsson join the Maple Leafs in a surprising NHL trade this season
articles.summary: NHL News: NHL insider Elliotte Friedman speculates that Erik Karlsson may join the Toronto Maple Leafs in a trade scenario as the Pittsburgh Penguins consider their options for the 2026-27 season.
articles.body: There’s an interesting NHL trade theory out there that Erik Karlsson could be a member of the Toronto Maple Leafs before the 2026-27 regular season. NHL insider Elliotte Friedman touched on the idea while looking at different moves around the league.Karlsson is in the final season of an eight-year, $76 million deal he signed with the Pittsburgh Penguins. There’s no confirmed trade talk involving Toronto, but that could change if Pittsburgh falters and thinks about moving the veteran defenseman. Erik Karlsson join Toronto Maple Leafs in NHL trade talks?If the Pittsburgh Penguins try to move Karlsson in the 2026-27 NHL season, he could be a trade target for the Toronto Maple Leafs.Friedman said on the 32 Thoughts podcast that he had been considering the move after returning from vacation. He said someone had predicted Karlsson would one day become a Maple Leaf, calling it a theory rather than a concrete trade development.The speculation continues to get attention as the Toronto Maple Leafs have been consistently looking to improve their defensive corps and build a roster that can make a deeper run in the Stanley Cup Playoffs.Why has Erik Karlsson become part of NHL trade speculation?Part of the reason this possibility has attracted attention is Karlsson’s contract situation. The 36-year-old defenseman is in the last year of an eight-year deal, leaving the Pittsburgh Penguins with a potential decision to make.If Pittsburgh falls out of playoff contention, the organization could theoretically try to move veteran assets instead of letting Karlsson’s contract situation get to the offseason without probing the market.What did Elliotte Friedman say about Erik Karlsson joining Toronto?Friedman described the Toronto case as a forecast by an unnamed source rather than saying that negotiations were underway.The insider said that projection was linked to Toronto's Swedish hockey connections, name-dropping the likes of Mats Sundin and Daniel Alfredsson when it came to why Karlsson might fit the Maple Leafs' orbit.Friedman’s response indicated he thought the theory was at least worth discussing, but there was no indication the Toronto Maple Leafs and Pittsburgh Penguins are actually in trade talks.How could Erik Karlsson affect the Toronto Maple Leafs?Adding Karlsson would give the Toronto Maple Leafs another veteran defenseman with plenty of offensive ability in the NHL. His experience and puck-moving ability could add another dimension to the Toronto blue line.The bigger question would be cost, contract considerations and whether the Maple Leafs believe Karlsson's production fits their long-term roster construction.For now, the story is NHL trade rumors, not a story that is finished. Karlsson would have to say yes to a move, and Pittsburgh would have to decide if a trade makes sense for its competitive direction.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Why did ESPN analyst Michael Wilbon criticize NHL star Connor Hellebuyck over his Winnipeg Jets trade request
articles.summary: NHL News: ESPN analyst Michael Wilbon criticizes NHL goaltender Connor Hellebuyck for wanting to be traded from the Winnipeg Jets despite having a long-term contract, highlighting the importance of player responsibility and ownership.
articles.body: The NHL offseason has taken a dramatic turn after Winnipeg Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck went public with his trade request, which he told the organization he had made several months ago. The move has left one of the league’s most accomplished netminders in limbo.Hellebuyck made his request public as training camp approaches, saying he feels moving on is the best course for him and his family. The Winnipeg Jets acknowledged his desire for a change but said there was no immediate update on trade talks.Why did Connor Hellebuyck request a Winnipeg Jets trade?Connor Hellebuyck’s publicly stated reason is his belief that his family should move on.Months before the situation became public, he made his first trade request in private, allowing the Winnipeg Jets to explore possible options.With NHL camps approaching, the timing became more significant. He wanted to do it quietly and respectfully, but I thought I’d confirm the request publicly, Hellebuyck said. His comments have thus moved the situation from offseason speculation to a major roster issue for Winnipeg.The request follows a tough 2025-26 season for the Winnipeg Jets. The team went 35-35-12 and didn’t make the Stanley Cup Playoffs after entering last season as the Presidents’ Trophy winner. Hellebuyck’s fears about Winnipeg constructing a championship contender were already part of the bigger picture when it came to his future.What did Michael Wilbon say about Connor Hellebuyck’s decision?ESPN’s Michael Wilbon ripped Connor Hellebuyck’s approach, particularly his wanting to be traded after signing a long-term deal with the Winnipeg Jets.Wilbon said that Hellebuyck should take more ownership in helping this team get better, not just demanding a trade. His comments were reflective of the frustration surrounding a star player who still has a contract but is asking the organization to find him another destination.The critique adds an American media voice to a story that has already been widely covered in Winnipeg and across Canadian hockey coverage. Wilbon’s comments were particularly pointed because Hellebuyck is still one of the NHL’s most decorated active goalies.Now, the Winnipeg Jets have to find out if a trade can be brokered before the 2026-27 NHL season begins. Kevin Cheveldayoff, the general manager, has admitted that Hellebuyck wants a change, but has also stressed the importance of respecting what the goalie has meant to the organization.Hellebuyck is in the third season of a seven-year, $59.5 million contract with an average annual value of $8.5 million, and that contract, his no-move clause and his recent play could make negotiations challenging.Hellebuyck, who has spent all 11 of his NHL seasons with Winnipeg. He has won three Vezina Trophies and a Hart Trophy. Additionally, his potential departure would thus be one of the biggest roster changes for the franchise in years.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Get to know our exciting new Brazilian signing a little better with a few facts about Allan Elias’s career and backstory following his move to Manchester Cit...
articles.body:
Get to know our exciting new Brazilian signing a little better with a few facts about Allan Elias's career and backstory following his move to Manchester City.

Allan's nickname as a child growing up in Brazil was 'Little Balotelli'. That was christened in homage to his bleach blond Mohawk hairdo.

However, in truth the nickname was more inspired by Brazilian icon Neymar rather than in reference to City's beloved favourite maverick Italian Mario Balotelli.

Allan follows in the footsteps of a number of other notable players to have made the move from Palmeiras to City.

Central defender Vitor Reis also joined us from the Sao Paulo club back in January 2025 whilst Gabriel Jesus also moved from Palmeiras to City early in 2017.

Lucas Andrade was Allan's coach at both Under-15 and Under 20 level at Palmeiras and reveals how he was first truly alerted to his potential during a youth tournament here in England when Elias was still a teenager.

"He scored a lot of goals," recalled Andrade. "But that tournament is when I realised Allan had the level to play here one day.

"He played very well against Chelsea, against Tottenham. The final was Manchester City against Chelsea. And I watched the game with Allan in the crowd. And now, many years later, he has come back to England to play for Manchester City. It is a very nice story."

After Elias had registered his first senior goal for Palmeiras in January of last year against Mirassol, subsequent TV footage of his parents' joyful celebrations went viral across Brazil.

Ahead of signing for City, Allan says he received hugely helpful advice and information from Brazilian compatriot Vitor Reis.

"He said that when I arrived, he would give me attention and talk to me and explain to me how it works," Allan revealed

City are signing not just a hugely talented winger but also a selfless player equally adept at playing as both a midfielder and defender.

"He's been playing mainly as a right winger since he was promoted to the first team, but he was a No. 10 [behind the striker] most of the time in his youth career," said Rogério Ferreira, former head of the Palmeiras academy.

"He can easily also be a [box-to-box] No. 8, and work on both wings. He has the versatility to adapt to style and different teams and pace."

Allan credits futsal with helping aid his early career progression.

He played the sport from the age of seven through to 14 and says the close skills and technique it demands perfectly equipped him for the challenge of mainstream football.

In the wake of a hugely impressive first full campaign with Palmeiras, Allan's impact was further recognised when he was awarded the Bola de Prata breakthrough award.

The prize recognises the young player to have made the most significant impact in the Brazilian top tier with Estevao and Endrick amongst the previous recipients.

One of Allan's most iconic displays to date came at Rio de Janeiro's famed Maracana Stadium in earlier in 2026.

He was part of a Palmeiras side taking on a Flamengo side who hadn't beaten at the Maracanã for almost 11 years. Allan helped change all that.

After setting up the opening goal, Allan then scored the second himself with Palmeirs eventually running comprehensive 3-0 victors and illustrated his capacity to produce in the most pressurised of environments.

As well as possessing excellent technical quality, Allan's character, personality and selfless mindset has also come in for praise.

"He comes from that generation, this latest generation of good players, good people, good characters," Palmeiras coach Abel Ferreira said last year.

"Whether they play or not, whether they are substituted or not, they understand and respect the coach. But more than the coach, they respect the group."

articles.title: Which bowl game does The Athletic predict for Florida football?
articles.summary: The Athletic projects Florida to return to bowl season in Jon Sumrall's first year, with an in-state matchup against an ACC foe.
articles.body:
After falling short of the six-win minimum to secure bowl eligibility in 2025, The Athletic projects Florida to return to bowl play in Jon Sumrall's first year.

Scott Dochterman took his shot at predicting every bowl matchup as the 2026 season gets underway, and he has Florida facing Duke in the Gasparilla Bowl on Dec. 18 in Tampa. Florida has played in the Gasparilla Bowl twice over the past five years, falling to UCF in 2021 and beating Sumrall's transfer-depleted Tulane squad in 2024.

Being in Florida, the Gasparilla Bowl would present a home-field advantage for the Gators. Dochterman also toyed with the idea of Steve Spurrier doing the coin flip between two of his former programs. Spurrier reached the top of the mountain at Florida, but his first college head coaching job came at Duke.

Despite Sumrall's public desire to compete for an upper-tier bowl selection, or even a College Football Playoff appearance, simply reaching bowl eligibility would be a sign of improvement for Florida in Year 1. The Athletic's Seth Emerson recently projected a 7-5 finish for Florida but noted that eight to 10 wins isn't completely out of reach.

Dochterman projected four SEC teams to make the CFP: Alabama, Georgia, Oklahoma and Texas. Three of those teams are on Florida's schedule this season, with Alabama being the exception. He also has Ole Miss landing in the Citrus Bowl, LSU going to the Las Vegas Bowl, Tennessee to the ReliaQuest Bowl and Auburn to the Music City Bowl.

articles.title: Could Auston Matthews strengthen his legacy as Maple Leafs captain through another challenging NHL season
articles.summary: NHL News: As Auston Matthews leads the Toronto Maple Leafs into a challenging NHL season following their disappointing performance last year, his commitment and leadership will be crucial for the franchise's success. Will Matthews elevate his legacy as captain?
articles.body: Auston Matthews is at the center of the Toronto Maple Leafs’ plans once again entering another season. Despite Toronto’s disappointing 2025-26 campaign, when the team finished 28th overall and last in the Atlantic Division, the captain’s job is safe.Matthews put up 27 goals, 26 assists and 53 points in 60 games, but his production dropped off late in the season. Now with Mitch Marner playing for the Vegas Golden Knights and Jim Hiller taking over as head coach, Matthews faces a new supporting cast and another major leadership test.Why is Auston Matthews staying with Maple Leafs?Auston Matthews is sticking with the Toronto Maple Leafs despite recent struggles because he’s committed to leading the franchise.Matthews ended the 2025-26 NHL season with 53 points, 26 goals, 27 assists in 60 games, including five power-play goals and three game-winning goals, and his production dipped late in the season, but those numbers still made him one of Toronto’s most important offensive players.Matthews finished his last 10 games with just one goal and five assists while being a minus-8. The slide was part of a bigger disappointing finish for the Maple Leafs, who lost seven in a row to close out the regular season.Maple Leafs enter another period of changeThe Toronto Maple Leafs finished 32-36-14 for 78 points and a minus-46 goal differential. The Leafs ended the season 28th overall in the NHL and eighth in the Atlantic Division.Big changes came around Matthews in the offseason. Mitch Marner left Toronto for the Vegas Golden Knights, taking one of the franchise’s most recognizable offensive stars out o Matthews’ supporting cast.Toronto also named Jim Hiller as head coach in June. His presence adds a new voice to the team and another element of uncertainty as the NHL season approaches.Matthews’ ongoing presence matters because the Maple Leafs are still working on building around their captain. Morgan Rielly is still a key defenseman after scoring 36 points last season, and Jake McCabe added 25 points.It’s not just about setting goals anymore. Matthews has to help Toronto respond after a season that exposed problems throughout the roster.Barring a change of heart, his decision to remain captain puts the onus on the team’s response under Hiller. Another mediocre season would only fuel the doubts about where the franchise is headed, while a more successful season could cement Matthews’ status among distinguished captains of the Toronto Maple Leafs.The Toronto Maple Leafs are led by captain and centerpiece Auston Matthews. The franchise is hoping to bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 NHL season that saw Toronto finish 28th overall and drop seven straight to close out the season and lose Mitch Marner to the Vegas Golden Knights.Matthews is entering another season with higher expectations for his leadership. articles.title: Could Misha Donskov’s Edmonton Oilers hire provide an NHL advantage over Western Conference rivals
articles.summary: NHL News: The Edmonton Oilers have appointed Misha Donskov as a coaching consultant, leveraging his championship experience with the Vegas Golden Knights and Dallas Stars to gain an edge in the competitive Western Conference. articles.body: Misha Donskov has been hired as a coaching consultant by the Edmonton Oilers, bringing with him plenty of experience around Western Conference contenders. Edmonton gains experience with two familiar foes from Donskov’s previous NHL experience with the Vegas Golden Knights and the Dallas Stars.The move could do more than just provide some coaching support. Donskov has NHL experience and has coached at the highest level, including Vegas’ 2023 Stanley Cup championship run. He has worked with theVegas Golden Knights and Dallas Stars before, so he knows two big Western Conference teams that Edmonton has faced often in pursuit of the Stanley Cup.Donskov has experience in both NHL coaching and hockey operations, so his job is a bit more than a typical coaching gig.He served as the Vegas Golden Knights’ director of hockey operations before being elevated to assistant coach. Donskov was on the Vegas coaching staff during the franchise’s 2023 Stanley Cup championship season.That experience is especially pertinent for the Oilers because Vegas has become one of Edmonton’s biggest rivals in the Western Conference.How could Vegas Golden Knights experience help?Donskov’s time with the Vegas Golden Knights could provide the Edmonton Oilers with more insight into the workings of a championship-level organization.The timing is interesting, as Edmonton was in the news recently when Vegas blocked former Golden Knights coach Bruce Cassidy from speaking to the Oilers about a coaching job. The difference with Donskov’s signing is that his previous NHL experience doesn’t give Vegas any say in whether he’s available for Edmonton.His knowledge of the systems at Vegas, his preparation and organizational approach could thus be a helpful internal resource.Donskov spent two seasons with the Dallas Stars in the 2023-24 and 2024-25 NHL seasons.His stint in Dallas adds another level to his resume as the Stars have been a perennial contender in the Western Conference. This gives Donskov a firsthand look at another organization preparing to compete in the same postseason environment as Edmonton.The combination of Vegas and Dallas experience makes the appointment especially intriguing for the Oilers.Donskov’s involvement with the Edmonton Oilers will be limited due to his commitments with Hockey Canada. articles.title: Gustavo Puerta da el salto a la Premier League, pero su destino inmediato estará en Grecia
articles.standfirst: Puerta, protagonista del cierre del mercado de fichajes en Europa
articles.summary: Puerta, protagonista del cierre del mercado de fichajes en Europa
articles.body: Gustavo Puerta está cerca de concretar un nuevo movimiento en el fútbol europeo. Aunque todo apuntaba a que el volante colombiano continuaría su carrera en Inglaterra, la operación contempla que inicialmente sea enviado a Grecia para jugar con el Olympiacos. De acuerdo con la información entregada por el periodista Julián Capera, existe un principio de acuerdo para que Puerta se convierta en nuevo futbolista del Nottingham Forest. Sin embargo, el plan del conjunto inglés es cederlo durante una temporada al equipo griego, con el objetivo de que sume minutos y continúe su proceso de consolidación en Europa. El futbolista nacido en La Victoria, Caldas, firmaría un contrato con el Nottingham Forest hasta junio de 2030. La vinculación le permitiría al club inglés asegurar los derechos del mediocampista, mientras que el préstamo al Olympiacos le daría la posibilidad de competir regularmente en una liga distinta y adquirir experiencia internacional. La llegada de Puerta también podría abrir la puerta a una futura sociedad con otro colombiano: Daniel Muñoz. El lateral derecho fue presentado este mismo lunes como nuevo jugador del Nottingham Forest, por lo que ambos podrían coincidir posteriormente en el plantel inglés. A pesar de que se habla de un acuerdo confirmado, el reporte inicial se refiere a un principio de acuerdo. Por esa razón, todavía deben cumplirse los trámites contractuales y médicos habituales antes de que la operación sea anunciada oficialmente por los clubes. Durante las últimas semanas, Gustavo Puerta había despertado el interés de varios equipos europeos. Entre los clubes que siguieron su situación estuvo el Benfica de Portugal, que analizaba opciones para reforzar su mediocampo ante la posible salida de Richard Ríos. Finalmente, el proyecto presentado por los propietarios del Nottingham Forest habría convencido al jugador y a su entorno. La fórmula contempla una llegada a largo plazo al fútbol inglés, aunque con una primera temporada en el Olympiacos para fortalecer su adaptación y darle continuidad competitiva. Gustavo Puerta llegó al fútbol europeo a comienzos de 2023, cuando fue fichado por el Bayer Leverkusen de Alemania. En su primera etapa fue cedido al Núremberg, aunque no logró sumar minutos de competencia. Posteriormente regresó al Leverkusen para la temporada 2023-2024. Bajo la dirección técnica de Xabi Alonso, disputó 10 partidos: siete en la Bundesliga y tres en la Europa League. Además, formó parte del plantel que conquistó la liga alemana. Para la campaña 2024-2025, el colombiano fue enviado al Hull City de Inglaterra. Allí tuvo una participación más constante y disputó 31 partidos en el Championship, en los que marcó un gol. Su buen rendimiento le permitió dar el salto al fútbol español con el Racing de Santander. En su primera temporada aportó tres goles y una asistencia en 33 encuentros, rendimiento que ayudó al equipo a conseguir el ascenso a la máxima categoría. Ya en LaLiga, Puerta disputó 34 partidos en total y logró debutar en la Primera División española. No obstante, su permanencia en el campeonato fue corta y ahora se prepara para iniciar una nueva etapa, primero en Grecia y posteriormente con el Nottingham Forest. La operación representa un paso importante en la carrera de Puerta. El mediocampista tendrá la posibilidad de vincularse a un club de la Premier League, aunque deberá afrontar primero el reto de competir con el Olympiacos. Su desempeño en Grecia será determinante para definir su futuro inmediato. Una temporada con continuidad podría permitirle regresar a Inglaterra con mayores posibilidades de integrar el plantel del Nottingham Forest y competir por un lugar en una de las ligas más exigentes del mundo. Por ahora, el movimiento se encuentra en la fase de principio de acuerdo, pero todo apunta a que Gustavo Puerta continuará su carrera europea bajo la propiedad del conjunto inglés y con un vínculo establecido hasta junio de 2030.

articles.title: Scottie Scheffler just won $10 million at the Tour Championship, so why was he craving a cheeseburger?
articles.summary: International Sports News: Scottie Scheffler ended his 2026 PGA Tour season with a $10 million Tour Championship win, but his first thought after the big payday was surprisingly.
articles.body: Scottie Scheffler ended his 2026 PGA Tour season with a $10 million Tour Championship win, but his first thought after the big payday was surprisingly simple. The world No. 1 said he wanted a cheeseburger, fries and maybe a milkshake. He also grabbed a rare beer after finishing at 16-under at East Lake in Atlanta. The win gave Scheffler his second FedExCup title and moved him past Tiger Woods on the PGA Tour’s career earnings list.Scottie Scheffler wanted a cheeseburger after his $10 million Tour Championship winScheffler entered the final round three shots behind Viktor Hovland, but he quickly changed the picture. He nearly made an ace on the second hole and caught Hovland with a birdie on the fourth. He then pulled away late, closing with a 4-under 66 to finish three shots ahead of Hovland.The PGA Tour said Scheffler finished the tournament at 16-under 264. Hovland was second at 13-under, while Ryan Gerard finished third at 12-under. Scheffler collected the $10 million first prize from the $40 million Tour Championship purse.After the win, reporters asked Scheffler what he planned to do first. His answer had little to do with the size of his prize.“Gosh, I don’t know. Probably a cheeseburger. I’m a big cheeseburger guy. Cheeseburger, fries… maybe a milkshake if they got one hiding back there,” Scheffler said, according to The New York Post.That was not the only small celebration Scheffler had in mind. After finishing his round and waiting to complete his media duties, he spotted an open bar and decided to have a beer.Scottie Scheffler celebrated with a rare beer before family timeScheffler said he does not drink very often, but the beer sounded good after the final round. He wanted to get inside for some air conditioning and had a few minutes before more media work.“There was an open bar inside and I’m like, ‘All right, I’m grabbing a beer.’ It tasted great,” Scheffler said, according to the Associated Press.His wife, Meredith, and his manager were surprised because they rarely see him drink.“Yeah, it’s fun. I don’t really drink very often. My wife and my manager were like, ‘Wow, I haven’t seen you have a beer in a long time.’ And it’s like, ‘Yeah, well, season’s over now. I’m going to have a beer. Well-earned beer,’” Scheffler said.Scheffler can now take some time away from competition with Meredith and their two sons, Bennett and Remy. His next major team event is the Presidents Cup at Medinah, which begins Sept. 22.The victory also changed the PGA Tour’s career earnings record. Scheffler now has $130,390,661 in official PGA Tour earnings, moving past Woods’ $120,999,166. The win was Scheffler’s 22nd PGA Tour title and his third victory of 2026.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Fantasy football takeaways from NFL's 53-man roster cutdown, injury updates and other trending news
articles.summary: Hayden Winks reveals his top fantasy football takeaways from 53-man rosters being set and other news.
articles.body:
Hayden Winks reveals his top fantasy football takeaways from NFL 53-man rosters being set and other news, with the start of the 2026 season just over a week away, to help you get ready for your remaining drafts.

Vikings, Eagles, Falcons, Steelers kept 4 QBs

This is extremely rare and unlikely to hold. The Vikings are very likely shopping J.J. McCarthy after he seemingly lost the QB2 battle to Carson Wentz as training camp played out. I'd think the Chargers (Jim Harbaugh was his college coach), Buccaneers, Jets, Dolphins and others will be involved. The same is true for Andy Dalton or Tanner McKee, as the Eagles don't need two quality backups to Jalen Hurts. The Falcons are waiting for Michael Penix Jr. to return, but I could see Tua Tagovailoa traded or released after NFL Network's Ian Rapoport said it was "impossible" to start Tagovailoa long term . The Steelers have a bunch of QB2 options and might be the most likely to hold onto all four, but once again, it's rare to keep four quarterbacks.

Packers placed RB Josh Jacobs on the Exempt List

I wrote about this extensively here , but long story short, Jacobs sinks to at least the 70s in overall rankings with the assumption being he'll miss six games or more depending on what is on this video. Lloyd is a no-brainer top-100 pick, even if he's a fill-in starter for the first month or so, but he has a pathway to being the Packers' starter all year long if things continue to turn for the worst. The Packers notably said they expect Jacobs to remain a Packer, however. Most teams take the suspension at face value and place a player back into the lineup after their return.

It's never a good sign when a former coach cites the current staff when calling a player "lazy", but that's what happened last summer when Blue was brought up. He never earned the trust of the coaching staff and was waived on cutdown day, despite some buzz that he could be Javonte Williams' backup. Blue never had that skillset. Malik Davis is the current RB2, and he has the early-down skills to be Williams' insurance. Expect Dallas to add more help here. That could simply be by signing Blue and Phil Mafah to the practice squad again. For now, Davis is a great last pick in deep leagues. Williams' doubters would struggle to make a convincing case against him at the Round 3/4 turn.

Jeanty's mysterious ankle sprain is now officially not that serious. If the Raiders knew he'd be out for the first four games, then he would've ended up on IR, but that did not happen. We should fully expect him back early on. Their season opener is against the lowly Dolphins, and Jeanty was only wearing a sleeve on his ankle when he rolled into the preseason finale in street clothes. I'd expect him to miss 0-2 games. The injury still has setback and efficiency risks. Mike Washington Jr. remains a quality late-round pick in fantasy but shouldn't be drafted inside the top 100 anymore.

Kamara's knee injury had a timeline of about a month, but the Saints expect him to be back before Week 4 at this point, if not earlier. The Saints have Travis Etienne Jr., Kamara, Audric Estime and Kendre Miller on the active roster. One of them will likely be a scratch each week.

Seahawks placed RB Zach Charbonnet on PUP

Not surprising. He had ACL surgery on Feb. 20 of this year. It was shocking to see so many reports suggesting he could be so far ahead of schedule that he would dodge PUP, but GM John Schneider said it wasn't a consideration to take him off PUP. If we follow the typical nine-month timeline, then Charbonnet will be back between Halloween and Thanksgiving. First-round rookie RB Jadarian Price will have plenty of time to establish himself before we see Charbonnet. He'll miss at least the first four games of the season.

Conner hasn't been able to practice with a foot injury. He wasn't going to be heavily involved on the Cardinals most likely, but Conner was oft-cited as a potential fill-in for other teams on cut day. That won't happen now. It'll be Jeremiyah Love, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight for Arizona to start the season.

Bucs RB Sean Tucker remains on team, took paycut

There was beat reporter speculation that the Bucs could release Tucker, as his $3.5M salary was non-guaranteed. Instead, Tucker is staying on the team but needed to drop his salary to a fully-guaranteed $2.5M. That's equivalent to low-end RB2 veterans like Brian Robinson Jr., Rachaad White, Isiah Pacheco and Samaje Perine. He won't be the Bucs' RB2 with Kenny Gainwell complementing starter Bucky Irving, but Tucker could have a miniature role as the RB3 in particular situations. Last year, Tucker led the team in inside the five-yard line carries from Week 13 on when Irving was back from injury. He is the biggest back, by far, on the depth chart, and it's unclear if he'll mix in on short-yardage, or if Irving will be an early-down bellcow while Gainwell plays on passing downs. I would've moved Irving up if Tucker had been released.

This was the analysis from long-time Chiefs reporter Pete Sweeney: "Moving on from Emari Demercado speaks to a couple things: the Chiefs see Ken Walker as a three-down back, and they love what Emmett Johnson has showed. Brashard Smith is a wild card Andy Reid can move around on offense, and he's KR2. Best return in a while for KC on Friday night."

I have Walker as a first-round fantasy pick and am fully confident in Johnson being a draftable player in the last rounds of drafts after seeing him in preseason.

Jaguars RB3 LeQuint Allen Jr. is on the 53-man roster. We don't have to pretend Bhayshul Tuten is gaining this pass-down role anymore. It's a minor injury.

Bills RB3 Ty Johnson (calf) is on the 53-man roster.

Dolphins released RB Jarquez Hunter right after trading for him. He's a practice squad candidate as he competes with Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon II.

The Lions have more RBs (5) than WRs (4) right now. One could read into this being Isiah Pacheco's injury could end up resulting in a stint on IR.

Ravens rookie RB Adam Randall was placed on IR, allowing Rasheen Ali to be the early-down backup to Derrick Henry, while Justice Hill is the rotational pass catcher.

Commanders rookie RB Kaytron Allen makes the team with Jeremy McNichols (quad) injured. He probably would've made it regardless but it wasn't a guarantee.

Colts RB3 DJ Giddens sneaks onto the roster. He's been behind RB2 Seth McGowan in camp.

The Texans "RB3" is just the fullback. That alone makes Woody Marks an interesting insurance play in fantasy.

Steelers rookie Eli Heidenreich is on the 53-man active roster, listed as a RB/WR. He's as much of a slot receiver as pass-down RB to me, but it's notable the Steelers don't have a "real" RB3. It's Jaylen Warren, Rico Dowdle, Heidenreich and a fullback.

Allen was arrested in downtown Indianapolis early on Sunday and was released later in the day. Typically, DWIs take more than just a few months to clear through the courts, and typically, the NFL doesn't suspend players for DWI until after the case is cleared. I wouldn't expect the Colts to release him for this, so the most likely scenario remains Allen just plays this year without a suspension.

Long-time reporter John McClain tweeted , "he's nowhere near ready to play" last week. This is the unfortunate reality for any professional athlete coming off a knee dislocation. We aren't even talking about a patella dislocation. No, this was his entire knee dislocating. Most players are forced into retirement, and Dell is now 24 months away from his injury and remains out of team contact drills. The Texans' No. 2 receiver job is a battle between downfield threat Kayshon Boutte, possession receiver Xavier Hutchinson and vertical slot Jaylin Noel. I'd draft them: Boutte, Noel, Hutchinson.

articles.title: John Cena Says WWE's Nick Khan, AEW's Tony Khan Don't Have Enough Money to Convince Him to Unretire
articles.summary: WWE legend John Cena isn't planning on ending his retirement from in-ring competition anytime soon.
articles.body:
WWE legend John Cena isn't planning on ending his retirement from in-ring competition anytime soon.

While speaking at a fan expo in Toronto over the weekend, Cena didn't let a chant for "one more match" go unaddressed, as he made it clear that neither WWE nor AEW would be able to afford him.

"I'm out, dog, whoever said that," Cena said (11:00 mark). "No Khan has got the pocketbook. Nick, Tony, they ain't got the money. I'm out. I'm out."

Cena wrestled his final match for WWE in December, though he's made a few surprise appearances with the company since then. However, it's been clear that the 49-year-old is prioritizing his acting career.

It wouldn't be out of the question for Cena to change his mind at some point down the line, as many wrestlers returned from retirement after they couldn't resist the call of the wrestling ring. But for now, it sounds like Cena won't be lacing up his boots again anytime soon.

articles.title: Alfredo Arias deja de ser el técnico de Junior de Barranquilla: ¿Quién será su reemplazo?
articles.standfirst: Junior oficializa la salida de Alfredo Arias y ya busca a su susrituto
articles.summary: Junior oficializa la salida de Alfredo Arias y ya busca a su susrituto
articles.body: Junior de Barranquilla confirmó la salida de Alfredo Arias como director técnico del equipo profesional. La decisión fue anunciada este lunes 31 de agosto, luego del empate 1-1 contra Independiente Santa Fe, resultado que profundizó la crisis deportiva del conjunto rojiblanco. A través de un comunicado, la institución informó que el entrenador uruguayo y los integrantes de su cuerpo técnico no continuarán en sus cargos. El club agradeció el trabajo realizado durante su etapa en Barranquilla y destacó los objetivos alcanzados, especialmente los dos campeonatos consecutivos obtenidos bajo su conducción. “Junior FC informa oficialmente que el profesor Alfredo Arias no continuará como director técnico del equipo profesional”, señaló la institución en su comunicación oficial. La salida de Arias se produjo después de un inicio complicado en la Liga BetPlay II-2026. Junior no consiguió ninguna victoria en sus primeros cinco compromisos: perdió frente a Deportes Tolima, Millonarios y América, mientras que empató contra Once Caldas e Independiente Santa Fe. Con apenas dos puntos, el equipo ocupaba la casilla 17 de la tabla de posiciones. Además, acumulaba siete partidos consecutivos sin ganar entre la Liga y la Copa BetPlay, una racha que aumentó la presión sobre el cuerpo técnico y generó fuertes cuestionamientos por parte de la afición. El panorama también estuvo marcado por la eliminación en la Copa BetPlay frente a Barranquilla FC, equipo de la segunda división. A esto se sumaron la eliminación en la fase de grupos de la Copa Libertadores y la derrota ante Santa Fe en la Superliga, resultados que terminaron debilitando el respaldo de la dirigencia. La salida de Arias representa un contraste significativo con los éxitos que alcanzó durante su primer año en el club. El entrenador asumió el cargo el 24 de junio de 2025 y rápidamente condujo al equipo a la conquista de la Liga BetPlay II-2025, tras superar a Deportes Tolima en la final. Meses después, Junior volvió a celebrar un título. En la Liga BetPlay I-2026, el equipo derrotó a Atlético Nacional y consiguió la duodécima estrella de su historia. De esta manera, el conjunto barranquillero se convirtió en bicampeón del fútbol colombiano. Arias se convirtió, además, en el primer entrenador que logró conquistar dos títulos de Liga con Junior durante su primer año en la institución. Sin embargo, el pobre rendimiento del semestre siguiente no fue compensado por los logros recientes y la directiva decidió ponerle fin al proceso. Durante su paso por Junior, Alfredo Arias dirigió 74 partidos, con un balance de 33 victorias, 18 empates y 13 derrotas. Su rendimiento global fue del 50,9 por ciento, además de los dos títulos que quedarán como el principal legado de su ciclo en el club. La institución resaltó que el técnico y su equipo de trabajo afrontaron el desafío “con profesionalismo, compromiso y convicción”, pero sostuvo que el fútbol está marcado por ciclos y decisiones propias de la dinámica de los clubes. Junior deberá definir ahora quién asumirá el cargo de manera permanente. Hasta el momento del anuncio, la institución no había confirmado públicamente el nombre del reemplazo de Arias, aunque el nuevo entrenador tendrá la tarea inmediata de recuperar al equipo en la Liga y encaminarlo hacia la pelea por la clasificación. Con la salida de Arias confirmada, la dirigencia rojiblanca deberá resolver rápidamente quién asumirá el equipo en plena competencia. El nombre que aparece con mayor fuerza es el de Sebastián Viera, exarquero uruguayo e ídolo de Junior. Viera es recordado por su extensa trayectoria en el arco del conjunto barranquillero, donde se convirtió en uno de los referentes más importantes de la institución durante las últimas décadas. Su conocimiento del entorno, de la exigencia de la afición y de la identidad del club lo convierten en una alternativa atractiva para la directiva. El exportero ya tuvo una experiencia como entrenador en el Real Cartagena y, según versiones de prensa, estaría negociando con Junior para asumir el cargo. No obstante, hasta el momento el club no ha confirmado oficialmente un acuerdo definitivo ni ha anunciado al reemplazante de Arias. La posible llegada de Viera representaría una apuesta por un referente de la casa, capaz de generar una reacción inmediata en el vestuario y recuperar la conexión con la hinchada. Su principal desafío sería levantar a un equipo que pasó, en pocos meses, de celebrar un bicampeonato a enfrentar una crisis de resultados.

articles.title: Why Red Sox broadcaster apologized for comments about Yankees' Jazz Chisholm, Austin Wells that 'crossed a line'
articles.summary: Red Sox radio broadcaster Will Flemming drew attention for controversial comments he made about Jazz Chisholm and Austin Wells during the team's series again...
articles.body:
There haven't been many bad weekends for the Red Sox this summer, but this past weekend was a bad weekend.

With a legitimate chance to jump the Yankees in the wild-card standings and remain in the AL East race, Boston lost three of four, concluding with a 16-1 thumping by New York in Sunday's series finale.

Red Sox radio announcer Will Flemming handled the drubbing poorly, making controversial comments about both Austin Wells and Jazz Chisholm that drew backlash.

Here's a look at what Flemming said and why he apologized on Monday.

Red Sox broadcaster apologizes for words about Jazz Chisholm and Austin Wells

Flemming advocated for the Red Sox to intentionally hit Wells with a pitch during Sunday's game as part of a tirade against Chisholm. Flemming was frustrated by Chisholm stealing two bases with the Yankees ahead by six runs in the eighth inning and made a handful of disparaging comments about the second baseman.

After claiming he received "nonstop calls and threats," Flemming tweeted an apology on Monday.

"Since I have been receiving nonstop calls and threats, I felt like it was important to hop back on here and say: My comments during yesterday's broadcast crossed a line. I'm emotional and a fan at heart and that bled into the broadcast," Flemming said. "I meant no disrespect to the Yankees players or organization. I could and should have used different words. These rivalry games get me fired up; I apologize for letting the emotion of the moment get the best of me."

The apology marked Flemming's first tweet since December, when he left the platform because it had become "toxic and negative" a day after he received backlash for hinting at a major Red Sox transaction that never came.

Here's a full look at what Flemming said about Chisholm and Wells.

What did Will Flemming say about Jazz Chisholm and Austin Wells

"Wouldn't you sort of like to see [Jovani] Moran drill Wells right here?" Flemming said to partner Will Middlebrooks, who was the first of the duo to call out Chisholm for stealing two bases after the Red Sox stopped trying to hold him on.

Flemming went on to call Chisholm a "bush league player" and said Moran, the pitcher, should have fought the Yankees second baseman after Wells hit a 2-run home run to make it a 9-1 game.

"I'm gonna say it, he plays the game the wrong way," Flemming said of Chisholm.

The Yankees would add seven more runs and close out a 16-1 win to take the series.

Flemming has worked for WEEI, which broadcasts Red Sox games on the radio, since 2019. He officially became the team's full-time play-by-play radio announcer in 2025, after Joe Castiglione's retirement.

Flemming's brother, Dave, calls games for the San Francisco Giants and has called both college basketball and MLB wild-card series games for ESPN.

The Lakers have limited options, such as Bruce Brown Jr., in free agency. They could also try to trade for players like P.J. Washington, Kyle Kuzma or De'Andre Hunter, but they might not have enough assets to pull it off.

Maybe they could focus on beefing up their center depth, which only consists of Walker Kessler and Kevon Looney. Sandro Mamukelashvili can play center, but he's more of a power forward and can stretch the floor.

Former Luka Doncic Teammate Named as Possible Option

GettyLuka Doncic #77 of the Los Angeles Lakers celebrates the 98-78 win against the Houston Rockets in Game Six of the First Round of the NBA Western Conference Playoffs at Toyota Center on May 01, 2026 in Houston, Texas.

According to Khobi Price of California Post , the Los Angeles Lakers could look into a former teammate of Luka Doncic with the Dallas Mavericks .

Dwight Powell is still a free agent and has expressed interest in playing at least one more season before a possible retirement.

"The most significant option for the Lakers could be Dwight Powell, the 6-10, 35-year-old big man who was teammates with Doncic for 6 ½ seasons in Dallas," Price wrote. "Notably, Powell has played the most games as a teammate alongside Doncic (389) among the 98 players Doncic has played alongside in his eight-year NBA career."

Price also named other veteran options like Drew Eubanks , Bismack Biyombo and Mason Plumlee . Potential trade targets, such as Jericho Sims of the Milwaukee Bucks and Jalen Smith of the Chicago Bulls , were mentioned.

After 11 and a half seasons with the Dallas Mavericks, Dwight Powell became a free agent this summer. Powell has primarily played as a backup center in the past three years, averaging 3.3 points, 4.1 rebounds and 1.1 assists in 63 games last season.

More than two months after free agency started, Powell is still available for interested teams.

According to NBA insider Marc Stein of The Stein Line , Powell is in constant communication with the Mavericks this offseason.

But with the Mavericks having 16 players on standard contracts, a return might not happen unless the franchise can shed two roster spots via trade. Powell provides veteran leadership and experience for a relatively young team.

Stein added that Powell is hoping to play at least one more season in the NBA.

The Los Angeles Lakers made plenty of changes to their roster this offseason. They officially moved on from LeBron James , who signed with the Philadelphia 76ers in free agency.

Here is the current Lakers roster heading into training camp:

articles.title: Fabrizio Romano: Leeds United star set for move to Serie A giants
articles.summary: Willy Gnonto to Fiorentina: Leeds United Agree Loan Deal With Buy OptionLeeds United have moved towards the exit of Willy Gnonto, with Fabrizio Romano report...
articles.body:
Willy Gnonto to Fiorentina: Leeds United Agree Loan Deal With Buy Option

Leeds United have moved towards the exit of Willy Gnonto, with Fabrizio Romano reporting, "🚨🟣 Fiorentina have agreed a loan deal to sign Willy Gnonto from Leeds United, here we go!" The update points to a deal that has accelerated quickly on deadline day, with the broad framework now in place for the Italy international to return to Serie A.

The key elements are clear. Romano states, "The verbal agreement is done with medical booked on Tuesday, as Sky Sport reported." That indicates Fiorentina and Leeds have already settled the principal terms, leaving the medical and final documentation as the next steps before completion.

From Leeds' perspective, the structure of the agreement is significant. Romano adds, "#LUFC accepted to include a buy option clause in the deal; Fiorentina cover full Gnonto's salary." That arrangement gives Leeds immediate wage relief while keeping a degree of flexibility over the player's longer-term future, even if the inclusion of an option suggests Fiorentina are positioning themselves for a permanent deal if the move develops positively.

Gnonto's Leeds career has contained flashes of quality, energy and unpredictability, though consistency and role clarity have often felt central to the wider discussion around him. A return to Italian football may offer a more natural environment for his development, particularly if Fiorentina can provide regular minutes and a tactical setup that plays to his strengths in the final third.

For Leeds, this looks like a pragmatic piece of business late in the window. Offloading the player's full salary matters, and the buy option creates a pathway to a cleaner resolution in 2027 if all parties are satisfied. For Fiorentina, they are landing a talented attacker with upside and limiting immediate financial exposure through a loan structure.

Leeds transfer strategy and Fiorentina move

This is the sort of deal clubs often accept when a player's future sits somewhere between potential and fit. Leeds are not fully cutting ties today, but they are creating room, reducing cost and preserving a possible sale route. Fiorentina, meanwhile, gain a player who still has age on his side and enough pedigree to believe there is more to come.

Assuming the medical proceeds as planned, Gnonto's next chapter looks set to begin in Florence.

From a Leeds perspective, this feels like one of those moves that makes sense even if it is a little frustrating. Gnonto has always had obvious talent, and there have been moments where you think there is a serious player there who could really make a difference over a full season. The problem is that it has never properly settled into something dependable for Leeds.

If Fiorentina are covering the full salary, that is a decent outcome straight away. Leeds do not carry the wages, the squad gets a bit more balance, and there is still a chance of a permanent sale later through the buy option. In that sense, it feels sensible rather than spectacular.

There will be some supporters who wonder whether Leeds are letting go of a player who could still explode elsewhere, and that is fair enough. But football clubs cannot keep waiting forever for every talented player to click. Sometimes a fresh setting is better for everyone.

The main thing now is what Leeds do next. If this outgoing helps create room for another addition, especially in attacking areas, then supporters will probably see the logic quickly. Gnonto leaving on loan to Fiorentina feels like a tidy solution, and probably one that suits all sides at the right time.

articles.title: Lando Norris Had ‘Interest’ From Other Teams Before McLaren Extension
articles.summary: McLaren driver Lando Norris inked a new deal with his long-time team until 2030, a decision that was easy for the current champion.
articles.body:
McLaren driver Lando Norris inked a new deal with his long-time team until 2030, a decision that was relatively easy for the current champion.

Norris has been at McLaren since his promotion in 2019. He is one of the longest-standing drivers on the grid, and he overcame his competitive demons to bring home a title in 2025 with the fastest car on the grid.

From their highs as a legitimate powerhouse on the grid to the lowest of lows as the slowest team on the grid, Norris has experienced it all with the Papaya faithful.

The British driver still has more than a year left on his deal, but over the last four months, talks of a new deal have been happening in the background.

May 3, 2026; Miami Gardens, FL, USA; McLaren driver Lando Norris (1) before the Crypto.com Miami Grand Prix at Miami International Autodrome. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images

Now, with the monkey off his back in terms of a title and a high level of confidence, he has recommitted to the British racing team rather than looking for a new challenge.

"There was some interest from elsewhere," Norris said in an interview with BBC Sport, "but I don't want to go anywhere. I don't want to be with another team. I don't want to spend time with other people.

"That's why it really was probably one of the easiest decisions I've made since being in Formula 1."

Why Lando Norris is staying with McLaren

Norris is only 26, and he is not even in his prime yet, giving him at least another 10 years of racing if he wants it.

McLaren, meanwhile, surely looks like they will be forever loyal to Norris, after coming up through their academy, becoming a champion, and staying faithful despite interest from other teams during low periods.

"The fact I stuck it through with them and then we went on to obviously have success certainly makes me feel like I don't want to… they didn't give up on me and I didn't give up on them.

"That just creates a very strong bond between everyone that works here. I want to believe that bond stays as strong as it is now 'til I do retire in my career at Formula 1.

"I know that's a long, long way away and I don't want to think of it. But I believe we're in the best place we've ever been even with a tough start to the season. And I believe that we can fight through anything together for sure."

Aug. 31—ROYAL CITY — The Royal Knights hosted the Ephrata Tigers, Moses Lake Mavericks and the Wenatchee Panthers for this year's football Jamboree. This gave each of the teams a good feel of how they stack up against players from different conference levels prior to their first game of the season.

"They played hard," Knights Head Coach Wiley Allred said. "Plenty of mistakes for everybody, I'm sure, but had some guys in there that haven't seen a lot of time, and it was good to see them playing. We kept a few kids out just because they need to get healed up completely for next week, and so we're excited to get those other guys an opportunity, and they showed up fine."

The jamboree was played by each participating team's varsity, JV and C-team squads, with both offense and defense getting 10 plays each against their opponent.

A standout player for the Knights on Friday was Dax Jenks, who looks to not have missed a step since a highly productive season last year.

"He was pretty special last year too," Allred said. "He's a little bit bigger, about 190, and he's a fast, smooth runner and got a quick twitch too. On both sides of the ball, he stood out a lot."

Much like a preseason scrimmage, the jamboree provides players an opportunity to become familiar with what the game speed will ultimately look like once the season starts, said Allred.

"We need a game or a jamboree like this," he said. "It helps everybody at least get a little bit of the nervousness (out) and then to not have the coaches on the field is actually a good thing. That pushes the kids to figure out what they're supposed to be doing each play. And again, having some different kids that aren't starting normally out there was really beneficial for them."

The Tigers new starting quarterback this season Cooper Vasquez was excited to get some experience ahead of the new season.

"I felt confident in our game," Vasquez said. "Felt confident with our line and our receivers that they could catch. Felt like we did pretty decent for the first time playing all together. There's definitely room to improve but definitely did good today."

Tigers Head Coach Patrick Mitchell also said the Jamboree provides an opportunity for players to get any errors out of the way now, where the stakes aren't as high like in the regular season.

"For some of the guys, it's their first true starting on varsity," Mitchell said. "First time out, you're a little bit nervous, but saw some of our younger guys settle down as the scrimmages went on and played really good ball, proud of the boys."

With four different teams participating in the jamboree, three levels of Washington high school football were represented. The Mavs and Panthers come from the 4A, the Tigers from the 2A and the Knights in the 1A.

Each team got an opportunity to play against each other throughout the event, providing players valuable experience of the types of teams they may encounter in their own respective conferences, Mitchell said.

"You never know who a team, even in your own league, is going to have," he said. "If they're big or if they're fast or whatever. It's nice to have that variance level of competition and just compete. Who cares who we're lining up against, we're going to go out and compete and give the best effort that we can, and we're going to do our stuff and be who we are."

For the Mavs, the jamboree was a great opportunity to tackle someone else other than a teammate.

"You can see some of the guys flying around. They've been looking forward to it for about 12 days now," Head Coach Kyler Haneberg said. "Going against a couple of really good teams that are physical as well gets us prepared for the season to come. Seeing those teams really helps, especially with Royal. They're really physical. They kind of match our physicality and our grit, and so it's really nice to see them every spring and every fall."

One of the big questions that surrounds the Mavericks heading into the 2026 season is who will take over as the starting quarterback after Brady Jay graduated. While they ran a few players behind center at the Jamboree, Haneberg said they are getting close to picking their guy — we'll just have to wait until their home opener against the Richland Bombers on Sep 4, he said.

"You can see the guys that get more reps than others, and so our offense is really humming with one specifically, and so we're really happy to see that," Haneberg said. "Especially today, going down, getting a couple touchdowns, and so we're happy to see that, and just kind of makes the decisions a little bit easier when you get against the other opponents, and they're making those great decisions."

Another standout player on offense Friday was Petrah Mackenzie, who got an opportunity to play running back, though he is typically on the defense at linebacker. With starter Elijah Burns a little dinged up, Mackenzie got a chance to show off his powerhouse style of running.

"He's a guy that some dudes don't want to meet in the hole," the coach said. "It's nice having him in there, and you can see those gaps open up right up for him, and he's going to run straight through those gaps, and anyone in his way."

With week one set to kick off next Friday, Haneberg and the Mavs hope to carry the energy they showed at the jamboree into practice this week and ultimately at Lions Field when they host the Bombers.

"Our practice can't dip it all," Haneberg said. "Keeping the energy all the way throughout the week, and our team does a really good job of that. Our captains are all hype energy guys, and so they bring the energy day in and day out, and so it makes it a lot easier for us coaches. They're a player-led program."
